thread:
infra-bot: [INCIDENT] SEV2 - memory creep in KV cache/paged-attn allocator observed across svc-serving-prod nodes in us-west-2. Multiple container restarts and a couple node flaps in the last 30m. Auto-escalating to on-call.

sam: seeing repeated OOMs on gpu-nodes-3/5. kube reports container killed, then pod back up. Noticing high frag ratio on /dev/nvme0p1.

priya: confirmed, alert spike started ~45m ago. Affected model routes: rtx-2-medium and rtx-1-large. Latency for those routes up ~2-3x and a handful of customer requests returned 503.

leo: attaching recent allocator output:
```
ERROR: allocator.cc:245 allocation failed, requested 1.2GB but free fragmented blocks sum=320MB
stack: PagedAllocator::alloc -> KVCache::reserve -> AttentionPager::page_in
CUDA error: out of memory (cudaMalloc)
```

ajay: copying logs from one impacted node:
```
kubectl -n serving logs pod/serving-rtx-2-7f6b9 -c inference-runtime | tail -n 200
[2026-11-05T09:12:03Z] OOM during kv page-in, freeing LRU shard 23 failed, slab defrag attempt 0/3
[2026-11-05T09:12:08Z] container restarted by kubelet
```

sam: initial mitigation proposal: 1) blacklist/evict the two hottest models from the affected node pool, 2) temporarily disable attention paging for rtx-2-medium to force non-paged path, 3) increase slab reservation to avoid small-block fragmentation.

priya::+1: on all three. Which is least risky to apply first?

leo: disable paging for a route is low-risk (config flip). Slab bump requires a restart of runtime pods on the pool. Eviction needs routing config change -> might increase latency for other nodes.

oncall-bot: @sam is now on-call for this incident. Handoff time 09:30 PST.

sam: I'll flip paging first. Priya, can you run the routing eviction for the two hot models to distribute load? Ajay, will need an increase in slab size and a controlled rollout.

ajay: starting with paging disable. Command: 
```
redwoodctl route update --route rtx-2-medium --atten-paging disabled --env prod --region us-west-2
```
Doing a canary on two pods now.

deploy-bot: Started rollout rtx-2-medium paging-disable (canary 2/2).

priya: routing change in progress: moving customer traffic for model: opensearch-embed-01 and convo-gen-x to other pools. Will throttle to avoid spikes.

emily: FYI CS: two enterprise customers (ACME corp, Nimbus) saw ~10 failed requests each. Logged tickets and gave ETA.

sam: monitoring memory metrics. Fragmentation ratio dropped from 0.82 to 0.61 after paging disable on canary. Good sign.

leo: slab bump proposal: increase default slab reserve from 12% -> 20% on impacted pool to reduce small-block churn. This will increase memory headroom requirement by ~8GB per GPU. Risk: fewer concurrent containers per node.

priya: ok to schedule slab bump but do rolling restarts across nodes with cordon/drain. I'll coordinate with infra to avoid simultaneous host drains.

ajay: implemented a hotfix to aggressively free stale KV segments on cache miss; deploying to canary. Patch: bump LRU eviction immediacy.

deploy-bot: Deploy ok: hotfix-kv-freeze v1.0.3 deployed to canary pods.

sam: note: observed one node flap during manual drain earlier — kubelet reported GPU driver reset. Not sure if related. Collecting dmesg.

leo: grabbing dmesg from the node, sending snippet: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (0x4e) at pc 0x00007f...
[ 12345.678905] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

priya: PCI bus resets could be triggered by driver OOM/sustained pressure. Let's keep node cordon slow and monitor driver logs.

emily: CS updated customers: we gave 2-3hr mitigation ETA and offered request retries. Both customers acknowledged.

sam: current impact: partial (some 503s), reduced after paging disable and hotfix, no new node flaps in last 12m. Action items:
- priya: finish routing evict and traffic shift (in flight)
- ajay: watch hotfix canary metrics for 30m, then promote
- leo: run slab bump rollout with cordon/drain plan (one node at a time)
- emily: keep customers updated with status notes

priya: routing shift done. Traffic distributed. No new 503s seen for 8m.

ajay: canary hotfix metrics look good: OOMs -> 0, fragmentation ratios trending down. I'll promote in 10m.

deploy-bot: Promoting hotfix-kv-freeze v1.0.3 to 50% of pool.

leo: starting slab bump rollout now. Draining node gpu-nodes-4.

sam: handoff note for next oncall (if needed): keep paging disabled for the affected routes until fragmentation stabilizes <0.4 and slab bump fully rolled. If fragmentation resurges, trigger full pool evacuation and reprovision.

oncall-bot: Incident status -> MONITORING. Severity downgraded to SEV3.

emily: escalations closed with CS. Customers updated.

sam: closing notes: root cause suspected to be a slow KV cache leak combined with small-block fragmentation in the paged attention allocator under certain request mixes. Hotfix reduces stale segment retention; paging disable reduced churn; slab bump prevents immediate re-frag.

priya: adding JIRA: KVSERV-5243 'paged-attn allocator fragmentation leak: triage and durable fix' and attaching logs.

ajay: leaving extra watch on metrics for 2 hours then will hand back to infra.

sam: thanks all. If any re-occurrence, reopen this thread or page oncall. :thumbsup:
